title: The Swing
source_note: NCERT structural alignment only. Zidd uses original teaching passages, checks, and feedback instead of copying the textbook body.

levels.title: Notice views from above
levels.focus: read visual clues in a poem
levels.teaching_goal: Use view clues to understand what a speaker can see from a swing.

guided_check.teaching_block: A poem about going up high often gives view clues. Look for things the speaker can see from above.
guided_check.passage: When Tara swung higher, she saw a river bend and a row of trees beyond the park wall.
guided_check.prompt: Which two things did Tara see from the swing?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: view clues usually name places, colours, or things far away.
bridge.passage: From the top of the swing, Asha noticed rooftops and fields in the distance.
bridge.prompt: Which phrase is a view clue?

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: separate movement words from seeing words. The swing moves up and down; the speaker sees the world below.
masterclass.passage: Rohan moved upward on the swing and looked down at the small green garden.
masterclass.prompt: What part tells us what he saw?

independent_check.teaching_block: Now find the view clue without hints.
independent_check.passage: The swing rose above the fence, and Nila looked down at the garden green.

levels.title: Infer the speaker's feeling
levels.teaching_goal: Use feeling words and evidence to tell whether the speaker enjoys swinging.

guided_check.teaching_block: A feeling word tells us the speaker's attitude. Pleasantest means very enjoyable.
guided_check.passage: Kiran smiled and called the swing the most enjoyable part of the playground.
guided_check.prompt: Which phrase shows that Kiran enjoys the swing?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: if someone calls an activity pleasant, they probably like it.
bridge.passage: Meera laughed each time the swing came down and asked for one more turn.

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: give the feeling and the proof. A complete inference says what the speaker feels and which clue shows it.
masterclass.passage: A child says the swing is the best part of the day and runs back for another ride.

independent_check.teaching_block: Now infer the feeling without hints.
independent_check.passage: Arun says the swing is his favourite thing at the park and asks to go again.
independent_check.prompt: What can we infer about Arun?

levels.title: Stretch a sentence
levels.focus: add details to make longer clear sentences
levels.teaching_goal: Build a longer sentence by adding useful details while keeping it clear.

guided_check.teaching_block: Stringing sentences means adding one useful detail at a time. The sentence must still make sense.
guided_check.prompt: Which sentence adds a clear object?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: ask what, where, or when to add a useful detail.
bridge.prompt: Which phrase adds where she watched from?

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: keep the base sentence first, then add where or when. Do not scramble the word order.
masterclass.prompt: Which is the clearest longer sentence?
options: Riya looked at the roof from the swing.
accepted_answers: Riya looked at the roof from the swing.
riya looked at the roof from the swing

independent_check.teaching_block: Now write the longer sentence without hints.
independent_check.passage: Start with: Mira watched the clouds. Add where she watched from.
accepted_answers: Mira watched the clouds from the swing.
mira watched the clouds from the swing

levels.title: Tell noun from verb
levels.focus: same word as action or object
levels.teaching_goal: Decide whether a word is used as an action word or a naming word in a sentence.

guided_check.teaching_block: Some words can be a noun or a verb. If the word shows an action, it is a verb.
guided_check.passage: The children swing their arms before the race.
guided_check.prompt: In this sentence, is swing a noun or a verb?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: if you can put a, an, or the before the word, it is often a noun.
bridge.passage: The swing near the banyan tree is painted red.
bridge.prompt: In this sentence, what is the word swing naming?

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: use the sentence job, not only the spelling. Same spelling can do different jobs.
masterclass.passage: We play after lunch. The play starts at six.
masterclass.prompt: Which sentence uses play as a noun?

independent_check.passage: A yellow swing hangs from the old tree.
independent_check.prompt: In this sentence, is swing a noun or a verb?

levels.title: Use position words
levels.teaching_goal: Use prepositions to describe where something is placed.

guided_check.teaching_block: A preposition shows position. Between means in the middle of two things.
guided_check.passage: A small ball is placed ___ two flower pots.

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: under means below something.
bridge.passage: The cat sat ___ the bench to stay in the shade.

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: picture the object first, then choose the position word. Beside means next to; above means higher than.
masterclass.passage: A kite is flying ___ the roof.

independent_check.teaching_block: Now choose the position word without hints.
independent_check.passage: The fallen leaf is ___ the swing seat.
independent_check.prompt: Which word shows that the leaf is below the seat?
